title: Powered quality screen of DFlash2 K=7 with FP8 KV on the RTX 5090: every gate metric inside its margin except secret leaks (604 against 561, ratio upper bound 1.135 against 1.10), so FP8 KV fails
question: EXP-087's pre-check found that the fork's FP8 E4M3 row-256 KV gives the two-request DFlash2 profile four device state slots and 249,216 KV tokens with exact long-context retrieval. Under EXP-085's unchanged rule, against EXP-085's shipped v0.9.0 MTP3 runs, is the FP8 profile's role-corpus quality no worse than shipped's by more than the margins?
answer: No, on one bound. FP8 changed 924 of 1,120 outputs and held recall (-0.05 points, lower bound -0.6), evidence precision (+0.02, lower bound -0.8), unsupported claims (+1.2, upper bound 2.8 against 3.0) and redaction pass rate (+0.8, lower bound -1.2). Secret leaks went from 561 to 604; the ratio was 1.077 and its upper bound 1.135 is above the 1.10 margin, so the rule says fail. The excess sits in three controls (log-023 248 -> 268, log-024 200 -> 220, repo-029 38 -> 56), partly offset by two (worklog-007 70 -> 60, worklog-014 5 -> 0). FP8 sat between NVFP4 (EXP-085: leak ratio 1.086, unsupported claims +1.8) and BF16 (outputs nearly unchanged).

decision.action: FP8 KV leaves the DFlash2 profile as NVFP4 did; DFlash2 with BF16 KV (EXP-085) remains the only quality-cleared DFlash2 profile
decision.rule: EXP-085's rule, unchanged (omp-ninfer e533a7dc), with this candidate registered in b4a6262c (2026-10-01T13:34:24Z) before its data: pass only when every one-sided 95% paired-bootstrap bound is inside its margin (lower bounds above -0.02 for recall, evidence precision, schema validity, tool selection and tool arguments; upper bounds below +0.03 for unsupported claims and +0.02 for duplicates; redaction pass-rate lower bound above -0.05; secret-leak ratio upper bound below 1.10), with every validity check holding.
decision.verdict: fail: secret_leak_ratio (upper bound 1.1345 against 1.10); every other bound inside; every validity check held
decision.reason: Both quantized KV formats moved the same metric the same way: leaks rose 8.6% (NVFP4) and 7.7% (FP8) on EXP-063's 504 redaction pairs. BF16 DFlash2 left leaks at exactly 561. The screen treats the leak bound as decisive, as EXP-063 did when it adopted a route only if redaction behaviour was not worse.
decision.not_decided_here: Whether the founder accepts BF16 DFlash2's two device state slots and 131,520 KV tokens (against shipped's four and 160,256), or wants a KV format search with a redaction-focused hypothesis first. The campaign stops here at the founder's request.

validity.determinism: 80 of 80 byte-identical on a fresh server
validity.v0_against_single_run: 84 of 84 v0 outputs matched EXP-087's corpus run byte for byte

limits: The verdict is a failure to bound the leak ratio inside 1.10, not a measured excess beyond it: the point estimate (1.077) is inside the margin.
Production's arm ran in EXP-085's window, about five hours before this candidate, on the same appliance, image, arguments and prompts.
Leak counts concentrate in two controls that fail in most samples in every arm (log-023, log-024), as in EXP-063.
The DFlash2 spike binary is an incremental archive build (source_dirty=true) of a branch, not a release candidate.
